raw_case_text:
A 27-year-old female patient was admitted to the First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University for recurrent abdominal pain. This patient came from pastoral areas and had a history of contact with dogs and sheep. She had no associated history of vomiting, fever, jaundice or weight loss. Physical examination showed mild tenderness in the right upper quadrant of abdomen. The results of liver function, kidney function and coagulation function were normal. The levels of tumor markers, including CA 125, alpha fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen and CA19-9 were within the normal ranges. The dot immunogold filtration assay showed that the antibodies of EgCF, EgP, EgB were positive and the Em2 antibody was negative. The abdominal ultrasound showed a cystic mass (about 6 cm in diameter) in liver and a solid mass (about 2 cm in diameter) in kidney. Computed tomography (CT) confirmed a 6x6cm lesion in the right hepatic lobe, with irregular margins, unclear boundary, calcification of the wall and heterogeneous density (Fig. 1A), as well as a mass with a size of 2x2 cm in the right kidney (Fig. 1B). Most of the lesions protruded from the kidney, and the lesion of kidney was significantly enhanced after contrast enhancement (Fig. 1C). Finally, she was diagnosed with liver Echinococcal cyst accompanied with clear cell renal carcinoma (Fig. 1D).
Then, pericystectomy of liver hydatid cyst and partial nephrectomy was performed. The typical hydatid cyst was observed when the liver lesion was opened (Fig. 2A). The hematoxylin and eosin staining of renal mass revealed large polygonal cells with clear cytoplasm, uniform round nuclei, and inconspicuous nucleoli, surrounded by a fibrous capsule (Fig. 2B). Immunohistochemistry showed positive staining for Ck7, P504S, CAM 5.2, CD10, EMA, CA9, Vim, Pax-8 and negative for CD117, which were typical findings of clear cell renal carcinoma. Albendazole was administered postoperatively for 3 months at a dose of 15mg/kg per day. The patient recovered well after the operation, and no recurrence was found at the one year follow-up.
Informed consent: Informed consent has been obtained from all individuals included in this study.
Ethical approval: The research related to human use has been complied with all the relevant national regulations, institutional policies and in accordance the tenets of the Helsinki Declaration, and has been approved by the ethics review board of Xinjiang Medical University.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 27-year-old female from a pastoral area presented with recurrent right upper quadrant abdominal pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was admitted to the hospital for evaluation of recurrent abdominal pain without vomiting, fever, jaundice, or weight loss.
subjective.past_medical_history: Resided in a pastoral region of Xinjiang with a history of contact with dogs and sheep.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for recurrent abdominal pain; negative for vomiting, fever, jaundice, or weight loss.

objective.physical_examination: Abdominal examination revealed mild tenderness in the right upper quadrant.
objective.routine_investigations: Liver function, renal function, coagulation profile, and serum tumor markers (CA 125, AFP, CEA, CA 19-9) were all within normal ranges. Dot immunogold filtration assay was positive for Echinococcus granulosus antibodies (EgCF, EgP, and EgB) and negative for Echinococcus multilocularis (Em2) antibody. Abdominal ultrasound identified a 6-cm cystic mass in the liver and a 2-cm solid mass in the right kidney.
objective.advanced_workup: Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT demonstrated a 6 x 6 cm heterogeneous cystic lesion with irregular calcified margins in the right hepatic lobe alongside a 2 x 2 cm exophytic, avidly contrast-enhancing solid mass in the right kidney. Following simultaneous hepatic pericystectomy and right partial nephrectomy, intraoperative inspection confirmed a typical hepatic hydatid cyst, while H&E histopathology and immunohistochemistry of the renal tumor (positive for CK7, P504S, CAM5.2, CD10, EMA, CA9, vimentin, and PAX-8; negative for CD117) confirmed clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Synchronous right lobe hepatic cystic echinococcosis (6 x 6 cm, confirmed by positive EgCF/EgP/EgB dot immunogold assay and surgical pericystectomy) and right renal clear cell carcinoma (2 x 2 cm, confirmed by partial nephrectomy histopathology and CD10/CA9/PAX-8 immunohistochemistry). The patient completed 3 months of postoperative oral albendazole (15 mg/kg/day) and remained free of recurrence at 1-year follow-up.
